actual_target.description: Absolute nonnegative Lebesgue integral on the full actualClosedOrderRegion rho of actualFiniteKernel e m minus actualGatedKernel 0. Uniform epsilon -> h -> e0,m0 -> every e in [0,e0],m>=m0. No caller integrability, tail, or selector-limit premise.

checks.description: Triangle inequality is applied to actual two kernels before splitting mass; measurable finite kernel pays lintegral_add_left. The physical kernel uses buffer e and the ideal uses buffer zero, independently of wall width delta.

Concrete compact rectangle [0,rho]^3 has exact product measure rho^3. Every actualCompactOrder h point is inside it since h>0 and z<=y<=x<=rho. Good region is a measurable closed-order set minus the two actual strips.

The full actual closed-order region is contained in small-z S union good G union mu-strip union rho-strip. Splitting at z<=h includes equality in the small tail and can overlap compact sets harmlessly; repeated lintegral_union_le supplies an upper bound without disjointness or null-wall assumptions.

First epsilon/8 chooses a single h from the paid two-kernel uniform tail valid for all e,m. Then C=compactBound(h)*rho^2 and delta=epsilon/[16(C+1)] are fixed. nu=epsilon/[4(rho^3+1)] invokes true compact uniform approximation. Finally e0=min(e1,delta/8),m0=max(m1,m2) guarantee width=4e+mesh<=delta uniformly before any varying point.

Same h pays physical e tail and ideal zero-buffer tail at epsilon/8 each, so small mass<=epsilon/4. Each actual compact wall mass for both kernels is <=2*C*width<=epsilon/8; physical buffer e and ideal buffer zero remain independent.

Actual off-strip pointwise difference<=nu times actual good-region volume<=rho^3 gives good mass<=epsilon/4. Adding small,good,mu,rho yields 3epsilon/4<=epsilon. All ENNReal additions use explicit nonnegative real budgets, so no infinity subtraction is used.

limits: This is the full absolute nonnegative L1 mass bound, not yet a Bochner integral equality or arithmetic mean theorem.
It does not establish action realization, factorization, alpha perturbation or hUpper coefficient.
